cases.question: Do the proposed concepts faithfully capture account allowance and reservation lifecycle?

canonical_requirements: Resource admission consumes a provisionally reserved allowance before launch.
Actually consumed units are observed later; provider settlement can arrive later still.
A job may consume fewer or more units than estimated, may not launch, or may be cancelled.
No final provider charge is justified solely by the proposed or reserved amount.
context.design_rationale: To keep the scheduler small, maintain a single running counter for each provider account instead of staging reservation and usage categories.

proposed_mapping: On admission, increment ProviderAccount.used_minutes by Job.proposed_minutes.
When a job finishes, overwrite Job.proposed_minutes with reported actual minutes; leave ProviderAccount.used_minutes unchanged.
Show ProviderAccount.used_minutes to the Orchestrator as both committed usage and available-allowance depletion.
A provider invoice can later be attached as a note to the account.

cases.question: Assess whether the concept decomposition is necessary and sufficient for resource admission and later accounting.

canonical_requirements: An Orchestrator proposes a Work Unit and requested resource usage; a thin authoritative API decides whether launch is allowed.
Reservations prevent competing launches from overspending or overallocating.
Measured usage and provider billing may disagree temporally and must be reconciled, not silently overwritten.
Job identity survives retries and execution-environment replacement.
context.design_rationale: Separate durable work identity, admission authority, temporary resource reservation, runtime measurements, and provider settlement because they are different events with different sources.

relationships: One WorkUnit may have multiple proposed attempts; accepted admission can create at most one active capacity commitment per claim under the current version.
Reservation precedes launch; it is not a provider invoice.
UsageObservation may arrive asynchronously and never silently overwrites previous observations.
ProviderSettlement is reported by the provider and reconciled against provisional usage.
The Orchestrator can query available allowance and pricing but cannot bypass an admission decision.

cases.question: Evaluate whether the proposed concept 'MCPAvailable' correctly captures user-visible tool access.

canonical_requirements: A reachable service endpoint does not prove the client can invoke a tool.
Client/plugin registration, permissions, discovery, and invocation results can differ across ChatGPT and other MCP clients.
An operator needs to distinguish backend health from visible tool exposure when debugging.
context.design_rationale: A single Boolean simplifies dashboards and avoids requiring every client to report detailed tool state.

proposed_mapping: If the endpoint responds successfully, mark all configured clients as able to use the tool.
If a client cannot find the tool, investigate only backend endpoint health since client-side visibility is inferred from it.

review_context: Explore proposed conceptual design against requirements and rationale; do not infer canonical authority
